ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two small particles of equal masses start moving in opposite directions from a point A in a horizontal circular orbit. Their tangential velocities are $v$ and $2v$, respectively, as shown in the figure. Between collisions, the particles move with constant speeds. After making how many elastic collisions, other than that at A, these two particles will again reach the point A?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circular horizontal track, with point A marked at the top. Near A there are two small particles, the left arrow points leftward along the tangent and is labeled v, and the right arrow points rightward along the tangent and is labeled 2v, indicating that after the two particles set out from point A, they move along the circumference in opposite directions. Reasoning: Let the circumference of the circular track be L. The two particles have equal masses, and when a one-dimensional elastic collision occurs, they exchange velocities; this is equivalent to regarding the collision as the two particles passing through each other and continuing to move at their original speeds. Therefore the “penetration model” can be used to calculate the meeting positions. The two particles move toward each other, and the relative velocity is v + 2v = 3v, so they meet once every L/(3v). Taking the direction of motion of the particle with speed 2v as the positive direction: at the first meeting it has traveled 2v·L/(3v)=2L/3, and the position is not at A; at the second meeting the position is 4L/3, that is, after modulo L it is L/3, also not at A; at the third meeting the position is 2L, that is, it returns to A. Thus before they again arrive at A and meet at A, they have already undergone 2 elastic collisions outside A.

raw_record.question_text: Two small particles of equal masses start moving in opposite directions from a point A in a horizontal circular orbit. Their tangential velocities are $v$ and $2v$, respectively, as shown in the figure. Between collisions, the particles move with constant speeds. After making how many elastic collisions, other than that at A, will these two particles again reach the point A?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: a circular horizontal track has point A at the top, with two particles starting there and moving in opposite tangential directions; the left-going one is labeled v and the right-going one is labeled 2v. From the text, note that the masses are equal, collisions are elastic, and speeds remain constant between collisions. Use the equal-mass 1D elastic-collision rule: when the two particles collide on the track, they exchange velocities, which is equivalent to pretending that they pass through each other without changing speeds. Let the circumference be L. In the pass-through picture, the relative speed is v+2v=3v, so successive meetings occur every L/(3v). Their meeting positions, measured around the circle from A in the direction of the 2v particle, are 2L/3 after the first interval, L/3 after the second, and A after the third. Thus before they again meet at A, they have had two collisions away from A.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个圆形水平轨道，顶部标有点 A。A 附近有两个小颗粒，左侧箭头沿切线指向左方并标为 v，右侧箭头沿切线指向右方并标为 2v，表示两颗粒从 A 点出发后沿圆周相反方向运动。

推理：设圆形轨道周长为 L。两颗粒质量相等，发生一维弹性碰撞时会交换速度；这等价于把碰撞看成两颗粒互相穿过并继续以原速运动。因此可用“穿透模型”计算相遇位置。两颗粒相向运动，相对速度为 v + 2v = 3v，所以每隔 L/(3v) 相遇一次。以速度 2v 的颗粒运动方向为正方向：第一次相遇时它走过 2v·L/(3v)=2L/3，位置不在 A；第二次相遇时位置为 4L/3，即模 L 后为 L/3，也不在 A；第三次相遇时位置为 2L，即回到 A。因而在再次到达 A 并在 A 相遇之前，它们已经在 A 以外发生了 2 次弹性碰撞。
